title: Compactlet: runbook harness for ephemeral adminlets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight runbook harness (Compactlet) and developer SDK to convert small operational playbooks into single-step, idempotent adminlets that can be executed from the Console, CLI, or incident chat. Goal: reduce MTTI for common repair actions, standardize telemetry and permission checks, and make ephemeral admin actions reviewable and replayable.
acceptance_criteria: Compactlet SDK exposes a 3-API surface for declaring inputs, pre-checks, and the idempotent action implementation
Console can render Compactlet actions with input form and run history via existing runbook UI
Each Compactlet execution emits standardized telemetry (run_id, actor, start/finish, outcome, error categories) to ops.telemetry and links to traces
RBAC gating: Compactlet execution honors role based policies and requires explicit approval when action is sensitive
Compactlet actions are revertible or annotated with irreversible flag; irreversible actions must require two-step confirmation
E2E test harness with at least 6 simulated Compactlet runs and behavior-driven checks for idempotency and telemetry
steps: Design SDK: python + typescript flavors; small adapter for our internal adminlet runner
Prototype on a low-risk repair (cache priming) and ship internal Console integration behind feature flag
Add RBAC & approval flow integration with identity service and audit log wiring
Implement telemetry schema and add to producer side in Compactlet runtime
Run performance / safety tests in staging and perform a tabletop run with SREs
Iterate UX based on PM and Design feedback, then schedule canary release to 10% of oncall flows
decisions: SDK languages: ship Python first (internal teams), TypeScript second — lowered scope to avoid splitting QA
Execution model: runlets execute as short-lived serverless processes routed through ops-orchestrator rather than long-lived sidecars — simplifies lifecycle and scaling
Telemetry granularity: emit structured events per run with canonical keys instead of freeform logs to make downstream alerting reliable
tradeoffs_and_risks: Surface-level runlets reduce friction but increase risk of accidental dangerous actions — mitigated by approval gating and immutable audit entries
Serverless execution model trades cold-start latency for easier isolation; critical-slo admin actions will map to a different path (pre-warmed pool) later
Adding both Python and TS SDKs increases maintenance — chosen to stagger rollouts to limit initial surface area
technical_notes: Compactlet manifest is a single YAML declaring schema, permission hints, and revert metadata
Runtime will perform pre-check hooks: dry-run validator, quota/limit check, and a short backoff retry wrapper for transient failures
Run history stored as immutable artifact linked to run_id in PermaStorage; small index in Console for quick lookup
Use existing ops.telemetry topic; add runlet.type and runlet.sensitivity as required fields
